# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Use accurate, precise tools for measurement.
3. Measure the level of pollutants such as SOx, NOx, VOCs, CO, particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10), and any other relevant air pollutants.
4. Record the date, time, and weather conditions during measuring.
5. Calculate the total emissions based on the sampling data and known production rates and processes.
6. Compare your measurements with local and international emission standards.
7. Identify the type of industrial activity and sources of emissions within the plant (e.g., stacks, vents, storage tanks, etc.)
8. Use proper units (e.g., micrograms per cubic meter (µg/m^3), parts per million (ppm), kilograms per hour (kg/h), etc.) when reporting the results.
9. Clearly state any instances where the measured emissions exceed legal limits or standards and determine the frequency and severity of such instances.
10. Comment on the potential
